candidates.review: Upright perched bird with folded wings and a long tail hanging down, but it reads as a generic crested woodpecker, as the brief predicted: a spiky sawtooth crest on the crown and nape (an acorn woodpecker has a smooth rounded crown), a thin needle bill rather than a stout chisel, a slim elongated body rather than a compact one, a long tail with a forked tip rather than stiff pointed central feathers. Despite "no branch" it stands on a fused vertical stub (the lower fifth of the model) that the toes grip, so zygodactyl toes cannot be checked. Eye is a raised bump. Topology: one watertight piece (post included), 0 open edges, 0.9% slivers; 1.9 units tall, +y up, bill toward +z. Build script would have to cut the stub below the toes and rebuild zygodactyl feet, flatten the crest, replace the bill with a chisel cone, shorten and stiffen the tail, and paint the clown face by landmark regions: little of the generated geometry beyond the body and folded-wing mass survives.

candidates.review: The reworded prompt removed the two faults it targeted: the crown is smooth and rounded with no crest, and nothing is fused under the feet (the bird stands on its own toes). It traded them for new ones: the bill is a long thin dagger, about a quarter of the bird's length (a woodpecker's is about an eighth, a stout chisel) and reads as a kingfisher or small heron; "standing on flat ground" gave long stilt legs (about 30% of the height) with three toes forward and one back, not zygodactyl; the neck is longer than a woodpecker's; the tail is short with a notched two-pronged tip rather than stiff pointed central feathers. Wings are folded tight along the back, which is right, and the body is slimmer than the compact build asked for. Topology: one watertight-looking piece of 20,802 faces plus one stray triangle (2 open edges), 1.9% slivers; 1.9 units bill to tail along +z (bill toward +z), 1.62 units tall, +y up, feet at y -0.81, symmetric about x. A build script would delete everything below the belly and add short legs with zygodactyl feet, replace the bill with a short chisel cone, shorten the neck, and paint the clown face by landmark regions; what survives is the head dome, the body and the folded wings, which the procedural buildWoodpecker already gives.

candidates.review: No trunk was modelled at all, separate or fused: the bird clings to an invisible trunk, so there is nothing to cut. It is the first candidate that reads as a woodpecker: smooth rounded crown with no crest, a stout conical bill about as long as the head (about 11% of bill-to-tail length; pointed rather than chisel-tipped), a compact rounded body, wings folded tight with sculpted coverts, and a vertical clinging posture with the belly toward +z (the trunk side). Faults: the head is tipped back about 45 degrees so the bill points up and slightly toward the trunk; the legs stick out sideways from the flanks like arms with the feet raised beside the chest, toes splayed and not clearly zygodactyl; the tail hangs straight down in line with the back instead of bending to brace on the bark, and ends in a notched two-lobed tip rather than stiff pointed central feathers. Topology: one main piece of 20,260 faces plus 15 stray fragments of 1-4 faces (28 open edges), 4.4% slivers; 1.90 units bill tip to tail tip along +y, 0.64 wide (x, legs included), 0.70 deep (z), symmetric about x (centroid x 0.006). accuracy_notes: Nothing adopted. The species is told by its clown face (black mask, white forehead band into a pale yellow throat, red cap, pale iris), the female's black band between forehead and cap, a white rump and white primary patch in flight, and a compact body braced on a stiff tail on granary trunks. Two Meshy previews both miss the woodpecker build: the first has a crest, needle bill and fused perch; the second a smooth crown but a dagger bill, stilt legs and anisodactyl feet. Recommendation: keep the procedural buildWoodpecker (with the face painted from the palette) rather than spend more previews; the face is painted from the palette in any case.
